mcqs.question: What is the Equator?

options.A: An imaginary line of latitude at 0° that circles the Earth midway between the North and South Poles.
options.B: An imaginary line of longitude at 0° that runs from the North Pole to the South Pole.
options.C: A line that divides the Earth into Eastern and Western hemispheres.
options.D: A line that passes through the North Pole only.

mcqs.answer: An imaginary line of latitude at 0° that circles the Earth midway between the North and South Poles.
mcqs.explanation: The Equator is the 0° latitude line that encircles the Earth exactly halfway between the poles. It does not run north‑south (that is a longitude) and it does not divide the Earth into east‑west halves.

mcqs.question: Which statement best describes the Prime Meridian?

options.A: It is an imaginary line of latitude at 0°.
options.B: It is an imaginary line of longitude at 0° that passes through Greenwich, England.
options.C: It separates the Eastern and Western hemispheres.
options.D: It is the line that divides the Earth into Northern and Southern hemispheres.

mcqs.answer: It is an imaginary line of longitude at 0° that passes through Greenwich, England.
mcqs.explanation: The Prime Meridian is the reference line for longitude, set at 0°, and runs through Greenwich. It is not a latitude line and does not separate the hemispheres; longitude lines together define east‑west positions.

mcqs.question: How do latitude and longitude together help locate a place on Earth?

options.A: Latitude alone gives the exact location of any place.
options.B: Longitude alone gives the exact location of any place.
options.C: The intersection of a specific latitude and a specific longitude pinpoints a unique location.
options.D: They are used only for navigation at sea and not for land locations.

mcqs.answer: The intersection of a specific latitude and a specific longitude pinpoints a unique location.
mcqs.explanation: Latitude measures north‑south position, while longitude measures east‑west position. Only where a particular latitude line meets a particular longitude line do we obtain a single, unique point on the globe.

mcqs.learning_point: Understanding location through intersecting reference lines
mcqs.question: A place is recorded as 20° N latitude and 75° E longitude. Which of the following statements is true about its location?

options.A: It lies south of the Equator.
options.B: It lies north of the Equator.
options.C: It lies on the Prime Meridian.
options.D: It lies west of the Prime Meridian.

mcqs.answer: It lies north of the Equator.
mcqs.explanation: A latitude of 20° N means the place is 20 degrees north of the Equator, placing it in the Northern Hemisphere. The longitude tells us it is east of the Prime Meridian, not west.

mcqs.question: Which of the following cities is located closest to the Equator?
mcqs.explanation: Latitude indicates distance north or south of the Equator. Nairobi, at about 1° S, is only 1 degree away from the Equator, making it the closest among the listed cities.

mcqs.question: A traveler moves from Greenwich (0° longitude) to a city located at 90° E longitude. In which primary direction does she travel?
mcqs.explanation: Longitudes increase eastward from the Prime Meridian. Moving from 0° to 90° E means traveling eastward across the globe.

mcqs.question: True or false: The Equator passes through the North Pole.

options.B: False – the Equator is an imaginary line at 0° latitude that circles the Earth midway between the poles.
options.C: False – the Equator is a line of longitude.
options.D: True – it divides the Earth into Eastern and Western hemispheres.

mcqs.answer: False – the Equator is an imaginary line at 0° latitude that circles the Earth midway between the poles.
mcqs.explanation: The Equator is the 0° latitude line encircling the Earth halfway between the North and South Poles. It never reaches either pole, so the statement is false.

mcqs.question: Why was the Prime Meridian established at Greenwich, England, as the 0° longitude line?

options.A: Because Greenwich was the largest city in the world at the time.
options.B: Because an international agreement in 1884 selected Greenwich as a common reference point for navigation and mapping.
options.C: Because it divides the Earth into Northern and Southern hemispheres.
options.D: Because it aligns with the magnetic north pole.

mcqs.answer: Because an international agreement in 1884 selected Greenwich as a common reference point for navigation and mapping.
mcqs.explanation: The International Meridian Conference of 1884 chose the Greenwich Observatory meridian as the universal prime meridian to provide a single, consistent reference for longitude worldwide. It was not based on city size, hemispheric division, or magnetic north.
